name: Proof of Estimate (poe-solana)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 14 app (app/), static export, pointed at this devnet program. Only changes: base path, the IDL generated from the program source at the same commit (the committed app IDL is from a later program version), and /poll/?id= instead of /poll/[id] so it can be served statically.
learn: A forecasting poll stores the crowd's collective estimate on-chain: make_estimate takes a lower and upper bound, records the midpoint (lower+upper)/2 and the uncertainty (upper-lower)/100, and each poll lives at a PDA seeded by the global poll counter, so new polls get deterministic addresses.
source: programs/poe/src/contexts/create_poll.rs L21 (poll PDA = ["poll", num_polls le bytes])
steps: Clicked through the hosted app (test wallet 8WVm…): filled Create Poll and pressed Submit, which sent register_user + create_poll in one tx
Then moved the estimate slider on the new poll card and pressed Submit Estimate: make_estimate
register_user (mints 1000 POEKEN to the new user)
negative: register_user a second time for the same wallet is rejected (user PDA already in use, custom program error 0x0)
make_estimate with lower 70 > upper 30 is rejected (u16 underflow in upper-lower: program failed to complete)
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): the new poll card then showed 'Yes 60%, 1 forecaster, 1 estimate' read back from devnet. Earlier read-only check: /poll/?id=0 shows the poll detail and estimate history.
limits: Resolving polls and collecting points need the poll's resolver; not exercised in this run.

name: Picassol (on-chain pixel canvas)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 12 frontend (frontend/), static export on devnet. Only changes: base path, devnet RPC, this program ID, and a 0-SOL fee on recolouring. Its MongoDB points API (pages/api) needs the author's database and is not hosted, so the points counter stays at 0.
learn: Each pixel of a 200×200 canvas is its own account at a PDA seeded by ["pixel", x, y]: create_pixel validates 0–199 coordinates and initialises it, and update_pixel re-derives the same PDA from the stored x, y and bump, so anyone can recolour a pixel but nobody can forge its address.
source: Picassol/programs/picassol/src/lib.rs L122-L123 (update re-derives PDA with stored bump)
steps: Clicked an empty pixel on sol.college/dapps/picassol-hackathon/ with an injected test wallet: create_pixel
Same click on a local copy of the same build (pixel 33,173): create_pixel
update_pixel → rgb(20,241,149), read back from the account
negative: create_pixel at x=200 is rejected with InvalidXCoordinate
create_pixel on an existing pixel is rejected (account already initialised)
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): the canvas renders 200x200 cells, and clicking an empty cell sent create_pixel from the app's own code, on the live sol.college page as well.
limits: Points/leaderboard need the author's MongoDB backend and its /api/updateUserPoints route, which a static host can't serve (the app's POST gets 501; the pixel tx is unaffected).

name: TrustLock (dead man's switch)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 14 app, static export, pointed at a program we built from switch/ at this commit and deployed fresh to devnet on 2026-11-10. Only changes: base path, output: 'export' and the program ID.
learn: A dead man's switch is an escrow PDA seeded by ["escrow", owner, seed] that holds SOL until a deadline: the owner must check in before the deadline to push it back, and once the clock passes it, claim lets the beneficiary drain and close the account. The program reads the Clock sysvar, so the rule is enforced on-chain, not by the app.
source: switch/programs/switch/src/lib.rs L10-L20 (initialize: deadline must be in the future)
lib.rs L30-L38 (checkin: only before the deadline)
lib.rs L40-L46 (claim: only after the deadline)
steps: UI: owner (test wallet 8WVm…) filled beneficiary + 0.1 SOL and pressed '15s Escrow for testing': initialize
UI: the same button's second tx, deposit 0.1 SOL
UI: owner pressed Cancel on that escrow: cancel, funds back
UI: beneficiary (test wallet AgrL…) opened the app and pressed Claim after the deadline: claim
deposit 0.02 SOL into the escrow PDA
claim after the deadline → beneficiary received 0.02118872 SOL, escrow closed
negative: initialize with a deadline in the past is rejected (InvalidDeadline)
claim before the deadline is rejected (DeadlineNotReached)
UI: Check In (+1 day) on an escrow whose 15s deadline had passed was rejected by the program: DeadlineExceeded (error 6002, lib.rs:33); no transaction landed
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): the wallet connected from the Connect button, the dashboard listed the owner's escrows, and create, cancel and the beneficiary's claim all went through the app's own buttons.
limits: A successful Check In through the UI was not captured: the 15s/30s test escrows expire before the extension lands, and a date-picked escrow was not created. The beneficiary claims from their own wallet, because the app's IDL makes the beneficiary sign claim.

name: gree (mint an NFT with Metaplex metadata)
app_kind: The fork's own create-solana-dapp React app (web/). The author's initNft code was commented out, so the 'Run program' button did nothing; we re-enabled that same code (same accounts, seeds and metadata values) inside an async mutation and wired the button to it. Also: base path /dapps/gree/, hash routing for static hosting, and this devnet program ID. The diff is in tests/devnet/patches/gree.patch.
learn: One instruction mints a 1-of-1 NFT: init_nft mints 1 token to the signer's associated token account, then CPIs into Metaplex Token Metadata to create the metadata and master-edition accounts, both PDAs of the Metaplex program (seeds ["metadata", metadata program, mint] and the same plus "edition"), checked with seeds::program.
source: anchor/programs/gree/src/lib.rs L19-L80 (init_nft: mint_to, then create_metadata_accounts_v3 and the master-edition CPI)
lib.rs L107-L131 (metadata and master-edition PDAs with seeds::program)
steps: Clicked 'Run program' in the hosted app with an injected test wallet: NFT Gp7Ncuci… minted
init_nft from the flow script: supply 1, decimals 0, metadata owned by Metaplex with name GLC-20240317
negative: init_nft again with the same mint is rejected (mint account already in use, custom program error 0x0)
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py): the app auto-connected, 'Run program' sent the transaction, and the page showed 'Minted NFT: Gp7Ncuci1Mb4FbuXjDtfLW9Penz6R5iLEhBYECYAkBEQ'.
limits: The metadata URI is the author's IPFS link; the Inventory page fetches it through Metaplex JS, which we did not check.
